nodes.label: Koppen Climate Classification
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Most widely used climate classification system developed by Wladimir Koppen based on temperature and precipitation. Five major groups: A (tropical), B (dry), C (warm temperate/mesothermal), D (cold/microthermal), E (polar). Uses letters for further subdivision. Based on relationship between climate and vegetation distribution.

nodes.label: Tropical Climate (Group A)
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Hot climate between tropics with no true winter (coldest month above 18C). Subtypes: Af (tropical wet/equatorial - no dry month, e.g., Amazon, Congo), Am (tropical monsoon - brief dry season, e.g., western India), Aw (tropical savanna - distinct dry winter, e.g., central Africa). High annual rainfall and temperatures.

nodes.label: Dry Climate (Group B)
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Climate where evaporation exceeds precipitation. Two subtypes: BW (desert/arid - less than 250mm rainfall, extreme temperatures) and BS (steppe/semi-arid - 250-500mm, grasslands). Found in subtropical high pressure zones (Sahara, Arabian, Thar), rain shadows, and continental interiors. Largest climate zone by area.

nodes.label: Warm Temperate Climate (Group C)
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Moderate climate with distinct seasons. Coldest month between -3C and 18C. Subtypes: Cs (Mediterranean - dry summer, e.g., California, Mediterranean coast), Cfa (humid subtropical - hot summers, e.g., southeastern USA, eastern China), Cfb (marine west coast - cool summers, e.g., western Europe, New Zealand).

nodes.label: Cold Climate (Group D)
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Severe winters with coldest month below -3C and warmest month above 10C. Found only in Northern Hemisphere in continental interiors. Subtypes: Df (humid continental - precipitation year-round), Dw (dry winter). Largest annual temperature range. Taiga/boreal forest biome. Covers vast areas of Russia, Canada, Scandinavia.

nodes.label: Polar Climate (Group E)
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Extremely cold climate where warmest month is below 10C. Two subtypes: ET (tundra - warmest month 0-10C, permafrost, mosses and lichens) and EF (ice cap - all months below 0C, permanent ice, Antarctica and Greenland). Very low precipitation (polar desert). Extreme seasonal day-night cycles.

nodes.label: Mediterranean Climate
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Warm temperate climate (Cs) with hot dry summers and mild wet winters. Found on western margins of continents between 30-45 degrees latitude. Rainfall from westerlies in winter when pressure belts shift. Vegetation adapted to summer drought (maquis, chaparral). Found around the Mediterranean Sea, California, central Chile, SW Australia.

nodes.label: Climate Change
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Long-term alteration of temperature and typical weather patterns. Current change is unprecedented in rate, driven primarily by greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuels. Effects include global warming, sea-level rise, melting glaciers, extreme weather, ocean acidification. Both natural and anthropogenic causes but current trend is human-driven.

nodes.label: El Nino
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean. Part of El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycle. Weakens trade winds, reverses Walker circulation. Causes droughts in India and Australia, floods in Peru. Occurs every 2-7 years. Opposite phase is La Nina.

nodes.label: Ice Ages (Glacial Periods)
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Periods in earth's history when large ice sheets covered significant portions of land. Last major glaciation ended about 10,000 years ago (Pleistocene). Caused by Milankovitch cycles (variations in earth's orbit and tilt), volcanic activity, and atmospheric composition changes. Sea levels dropped 100+ meters during peak glaciation.

nodes.label: Milankovitch Cycles
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Variations in earth's orbital parameters that affect climate over thousands of years. Three cycles: eccentricity (shape of orbit, ~100,000 years), obliquity (tilt of axis, ~41,000 years), and precession (wobble of axis, ~26,000 years). Trigger ice ages by changing distribution of solar radiation. Named after Serbian scientist.

nodes.label: Acid Rain
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Rainfall with pH below 5.6 caused by sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides reacting with atmospheric moisture. Sources: fossil fuel combustion, industrial emissions, vehicle exhaust. Damages forests, acidifies lakes (killing aquatic life), corrodes buildings and monuments (like Taj Mahal). Transboundary pollution issue.

nodes.label: La Nina
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Periodic cooling of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean. Strengthens trade winds and Walker circulation. Generally associated with good monsoon rainfall in India. Causes floods in Australia and droughts in South America. Opposite of El Nino.
